title: Version Comparison / Security Diff - 'preprocess' mode output
description: Reference shape for scripts/diff_reports.py's `preprocess` mode: a purely structural diff between two raw preprocess.py JSON outputs (Step 3 only - no AI-authored findings involved at all), for a V1/V2 pair the user/workflow has explicitly declared - diff_reports.py never infers that relationship itself. Like report-schema.json, this document is the authoritative human/AI-facing reference; it is not executed by a JSON Schema library at runtime (see docs/decisiones.md D-054).

sameInput.description: True only when both sides carry the same non-null inputHash.

note.description: Fixed English sentence: structural facts, never a security conclusion by themselves (rule R-D1).

modifierScopeNote.description: Fixed English sentence: modifier/permission changes here cover only NAMED modifiers on a function's own declaration - inline body-level checks (a bare require(...) with no modifier) are not present in preprocess.py's public JSON and are invisible to this diff (rule R-D4).

renameNote.description: Fixed English sentence: contract identity is file+name; a rename/move is always one removal plus one addition, never inferred (rule R-D5).

contractsAdded.description: Contract `key` (systemGraph's own "file#Name") values present only in V2.

contractsRemoved.description: Contract `key` values present only in V1.

contractsMatched.description: Contract `key` values present on both sides - the only contracts functionSurfaceDelta reports on.

functionSurfaceDelta.description: Keyed by matched contract `key`. Only matched contracts are reported - an added/removed contract's own functions are implicitly all-added/all-removed and are not individually enumerated a second time.

functionIdentity.description: "kind:name(canonicalType1,canonicalType2,...)" - a local, independent re-derivation of preprocess.py's own selector-clash canonical signature, generalized to every visibility (so internal/private functions, which have no ABI selector, still get a stable identity - rule R-D... see decisiones.md D-054 decision 4). Never present when any parameter type cannot be canonicalized with confidence (a struct/enum/contract type) - such a function is unresolved instead (see unresolvedFunctionsV1/V2), never guessed.

functionsChanged.description: Functions matched by identity on both sides whose visibility, mutability, virtual, override, or applied-modifier-name set differs.

edgesAdded.description: Full systemGraph edge objects ({kind, from, to, function?, method?}), present in V2's graph but not V1's, by exact (kind, from, to, function, method) identity - never a fuzzy match.

systemGraphDelta.description: 'not_computed' whenever EITHER side's own systemGraph.status is not 'computed' (i.e. either run was not 'pro' mode / config/modes.json allowSystemGraph - the SAME existing gate, reused as-is, never duplicated - rule R-D6).

businessRules: R-D1: structural facts, never a security conclusion by themselves (see version-diff-reports-schema.json R-D1).

R-D4: modifier/permission changes here are limited to NAMED modifiers (fn.modifiers) because that is all preprocess.py's public JSON (to_public, which strips every underscore-prefixed field including the raw function body) retains; inline require()-shaped guards are not visible to this mode.

R-D5: contract identity is exactly systemGraph's own node key (file#name). A rename or file move is reported as one entry in contractsRemoved plus one in contractsAdded - never a single 'renamed' entry - matching the same 'never invent a relationship the data does not state' principle applied to the V1/V2 pairing itself.
R-D6: systemGraphDelta reuses systemGraph.status exactly as preprocess.py already computed it; this script adds no new mode-gating logic and no new config/modes.json flag.
